outcome: Mode of birth (cesarean section vs. vaginal)
cohort: The study included 90 children aged 7-18, both with and without misophonia, along with their mothers.
finding: Children with misophonia showed age-related differences in trigger response (aggression in younger, self-harm in adolescents) and had significantly higher symptoms of anxiety, depression, OCD, migraines, and psychosomatic complaints compared to peers, with their mothers also reporting more frequent postpartum depression.
mod_finding: Children with misophonia did not differ from their peers based on being delivered via cesarean section.
